documents.t: A plugin is an add-on code which provides functionality to cordova app or more precisely cordova web view to communicate with native components or in easy words it is used to provide additional features to cordova app. There are various plugins , few example below Phonegap-plugin-barcodescanner - to scan barcode Cordova-plugin-file-transfer - to upload and download files For adding plugin run command cordova plugin add <plugin-name> For removing plugin run command cordova plugin rm <plugin-name> Example - Cordova plugin add Phonegap-plugin-barcodescanner Note : Sometimes plugins are not compatible with dependent plugins . Then we have to use - - force at the end of command to add plugins forcefully. Example: Cordova plugin add Phonegap-plugin-barcodescanner - -force

documents.t: Open site - https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/analyze.html Enter your domain name in the input box labeled "Hostname" and wait for the web application to display the result. Under Server key and Certificate and additional certificates section look for Pin SHA256 label There will be 4 such labels. Collect all their values and store them temporarily. Values are marked in yellow as shown in the image. Now Open folder - platforms/android/app/src/main/res/xml Create on file in that folder with name network_security_config.xml Copy and paste the following content into that file: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?> <network-security-config> <domain-config> <domain includeSubdomains="true">procify.com</domain> <pin-set> <pin digest="SHA-256">VZbCxPHWEHQfBSK5uCQZqIbQ57dTkQCbY0SHQAAoI+M=</pin> <pin digest="SHA-256">JSMzqOOrtyOT1kmau6zKhgT676hGgczD5VMdRMyJZFA=</pin> <pin digest="SHA-256">++MBgDH5WGvL9Bcn5Be30cRcL0f5O+NyoXuWtQdX1aI=</pin> <pin digest="SHA-256">KwccWaCgrnaw6tsrrSO61FgLacNgG2MMLq8GE6+oP5I=</pin> </pin-set> </domain-config> </network-security-config> "procify.com" is the package name, which can be found in the google-services.json file In the previous 3 or 4 steps, you have collected three values for the SHA256 Pin. Replace collected values in four <pin digest=”SHA-256”> </pin> tags respectively. documents.t: A .certSigningRequest file is a critical part of the certificate generation process in iOS development. It is used to create a code-signing certificate, which is necessary for signing your iOS apps for distribution via In-House or Ad Hoc methods. The CSR file contains information about the developer or the organization, including the public key, which is used by Apple to generate the appropriate signing certificate.If you want to create a new Certificate, then follow the steps below. Open the keychain Access as shown in the below screenshot. Click on Request a Certificate From a Certificate Authority as shown in the below screenshot. Click on Keychain Access as shown in the below screenshot. Fill the below details as shown in the below screenshot. The user's email address plays an indirect role in the code-signing process since it is linked to your Apple Developer account and included in the signing certificate's metadata. While the Keychain holds the signing certificate and private key, it does not store the email address in plain text. Instead, the email is embedded within the certificate's metadata, which identifies the developer or organization. In short: Email is used to identify the developer in the signing certificate. Keychain stores the certificate and private key needed for signing the app, enabling secure app distribution and code signing. The CA Email Address is a part of the Issuer information within a certificate and provides a way to contact the Certificate Authority that issued the certificate. It serves as a point of contact for issues related to the certificate, such as validation, renewal, or revocation. You can find the CA's email address in the certificate metadata, which can be inspected in various tools like Keychain Access on macOS or by viewing the certificate details in a web browser. Once the build is triggered, it will appear in the location shown in the image below. Here you can also find the number of errors that came during the build. Once you click on the error, you will be taken to the error log (list of errors). You will see the error line. You are required to delete the error code. Note: delete the error code. Once the code is deleted the screen looks like this. Once the code is removed, clean the build folder. Once again click on the build. Once the process is completed, the logs will be visible in the screen below. Note: These logs are from Xcode. Open the .xcworkspace ( This step is Only for the FCM plugin ) And click on the run button (This step is Only for the FCM plugin). To debug from Safari, go to Develop> ipad> localhost.

Select the Automatically manage signing and click the next button. Click the Export button to export to your folder. Select the folder location and export it. Check your folder; your IPA is ready.
